title: 360. Fear City: New York in the 1970s

sentences.en: Ivy Stevens had been looking forward to the 13th of July for weeks.
sentences.zh: 艾薇·史蒂文斯（Ivy Stevens）几周来一直期盼着7月13日的到来。

sentences.en: She and her husband had planned their big night out long in advance.
sentences.zh: 她和丈夫很早就计划好了这次隆重的约会夜。

sentences.en: And as it approached, it was hard not to be excited.
sentences.zh: 随着日子临近，她很难不感到兴奋。

sentences.en: It had been a dreadfully muggy, oppressive day, with temperatures heading well into the 90s, and Manhattan's crowded streets sweltered with noise and sweat and heat.
sentences.zh: 那天天气闷热得可怕，令人透不过气，气温直逼90华氏度（约32摄氏度以上），曼哈顿拥挤的街道上充斥着喧嚣、汗水与热浪。

sentences.en: It was still dreadfully hot and humid that evening, and it was a relief, therefore, for Ivy to walk into the air-conditioned light and coolness of the World Trade Center,
sentences.zh: 那天傍晚依然闷热潮湿，因此，当艾薇走入世界贸易中心那充满空调冷气的光明与清凉中时，她感到如释重负，

sentences.en: its gleaming towers still only a few years old, and ride the elevator 107 floors up to Windows on the World, the elegant restaurant that looked out across the city.
sentences.zh: 其波光粼粼的大楼落成才短短几年，她搭乘电梯上升107层，来到了“世界之窗”（Windows on the World），那是那家俯瞰全城的优雅餐厅。

sentences.en: And of course, the evening was every bit as exceptional and memorable as she had hoped.
sentences.zh: 当然，这个夜晚正如她所希望的那样，无比非凡且令人难忘。

sentences.en: From her table, she could see the whole of the city laid out beneath her, a patterned blanket of blinking lights beneath a darkening sky.
sentences.zh: 从她的座位望去，整个城市尽收眼底，在渐暗的天空下，闪烁的灯光织成了一张图案错落的毯子。

sentences.en: It was amazing, she said later.
sentences.zh: 她后来回忆说，这太奇妙了。

sentences.en: We were looking out at the most spectacular view in the world,
sentences.zh: 我们正眺望着世界上最壮观的景色，

sentences.en: New York at night, when suddenly it disappeared.
sentences.zh: 夜色中的纽约，然而它突然消失了。

sentences.zh: 好了，多米尼克·桑德布鲁克（Dominic Sandbrook），这段话是一位研究1970年代美国的顶尖历史学家写的。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.zh: 出自他的鸿篇巨制《怒不可遏》（Mad as Hell）。

sentences.zh: 我想，这位作者当时受委托写14万字，结果最后写了50万字。

sentences.en: So, hundreds of thousands of words had to be cut.
sentences.zh: 所以，有几十万字不得不被删掉。

sentences.zh: 听众们可能还记得我们做过两期关于西贡陷落的节目，当时我们差不多是把那些你不得不删掉的章节给“废物利用”了。

sentences.zh: 关于停电本身的故事，我们先从这里讲起，然后我们会将其铺展开来，谈谈70年代纽约的犯罪和政治，那是一个迷人的故事。

sentences.zh: 所以在60和70年代，纽约及其同类城市偶尔确实会遭遇停电和所谓的限电（brownouts）。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，任何在盛夏去过纽约的人都知道，那里会闷热得令人窒息，

sentences.zh: 空气中酝酿着雷暴，这正是1977年7月这天晚上所发生的事情。

sentences.zh: 当时有一家特定的公司为纽约提供电力，即联合爱迪生公司（Con Ed, Consolidated Edison）。

sentences.zh: 当天该公司有一位系统调度员名叫威廉·杜里夫（William Durith）。

sentences.en: He basically is in charge of blacking out individual bits of the city to reduce demand on the other power lines so that the power lines won't burn out.
sentences.zh: 他基本上负责切断城市各个片区的供电，以减轻其他输电线路上的负荷，防止输电线路烧毁。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: He has very bad luck because he's fiddling with the lines and then lightning strikes again and knocks out another line.

sentences.en: Now, what that means is that the remaining lines are carrying more load than they can bear and they start to burn out.

sentences.en: Unless you reduce the demand, then more lines will burn out.
sentences.zh: 除非你减少需求，否则会有更多的线路被烧毁。

sentences.en: And that, of course, piles more pressure on the lines that are remaining.
sentences.zh: 当然，这会给剩下的线路施加更大的压力。

sentences.en: And you're into a situation where they'll all burn out.
sentences.zh: 于是你陷入了一种它们全都会被烧毁的局面。

sentences.en: God, this is so impressive.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这太让人印象深刻了。

sentences.en: This is absolutely very detailed knowledge, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是非常详细的专业知识，汤姆。

sentences.en: Tom, the power pool dispatcher of New York State, a man called William Kennedy, he rings Durif and he says to him,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，纽约州的电力联营调度员，一个名叫威廉·肯尼迪（William Kennedy）的人，他给杜里夫打电话并对他说，

sentences.en: you've got to start shutting bits of the city down because otherwise the whole thing is going to blow.
sentences.zh: 你必须开始关闭城市的某些片区，否则整个系统就要彻底炸了。

sentences.zh: 所以曼哈顿的情况很糟糕。

sentences.en: It's bad in Manhattan, but it's worse.
sentences.zh: 曼哈顿很糟，但更糟的是

sentences.en: In the Bronx.
sentences.zh: 在布朗克斯。

sentences.en: So in the Bronx, 473 shops attacked, 961 looters are arrested.
sentences.zh: 所以在布朗克斯，473家店铺遭到袭击，961名暴徒被捕。

sentences.en: There's an Ace Pontiac car showroom, and 200 people force their way into the showroom, and Because of the drive-off.
sentences.zh: 有一家王牌庞蒂亚克（Ace Pontiac）汽车展厅，200人强行闯入展厅，因为可以直接把车开走。

sentences.en: And they just drive off with the cars.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就这样把车开走了。

sentences.en: They drive off with 50 cars.
sentences.zh: 他们开走了50辆汽车。

sentences.en: One by one.
sentences.zh: 一辆接一辆。

sentences.en: In a sort of single file, through the glass, out into the street.
sentences.zh: 众人排成单行，穿过玻璃门，来到街上。

sentences.en: Brooklyn, even worse than the Bronx.
sentences.zh: 布鲁克林，甚至比布朗克斯还要糟糕。

sentences.en: So 700 stores in Brooklyn were gutted, looted, burned, 1,000 people arrested.
sentences.zh: 因此，布鲁克林有700家店铺被洗劫、抢空并焚毁，1000人被捕。

sentences.en: And there's one neighborhood in particular that becomes synonymous with the blackout of 1977.
sentences.zh: 有一个社区尤其成为了1977年大停电的代名词。

sentences.en: It's called Bushwick.
sentences.zh: 它叫布什威克。

sentences.en: So Bushwick is off in northeastern Brooklyn, and by this point, it is predominantly black and Puerto Rican.
sentences.zh: 布什威克位于布鲁克林东北部，到这个时候，居民已经以黑人和波多黎各人为主了。

sentences.en: And we'll talk a little bit later in the podcast about these neighborhoods where the demography had changed massively in the 1960s and 1970s.
sentences.zh: 我们在稍后的播客中会谈到这些社区，它们在20世纪60和70年代经历了巨幅的人口结构变化。

sentences.en: So Bushwick, already in the 70s, had a reputation for very high levels of people on welfare, very high levels of violence, vandalism.
sentences.zh: 所以在70年代，布什威克就已经以极高比例的吃救济人口、极高的暴力率和破坏行为而闻名。

sentences.en: It's basically not a place where tourists go, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这里基本上不是游客会去的地方。

sentences.en: So it's the kind of the reaches of Gotham City that Batman would be clearing up.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是哥谭市里蝙蝠侠会去清理的那种地方。

sentences.en: The Batman would be clearing up, or Batman might be slightly out of his depth, though, I say, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，不过我觉得，蝙蝠侠去清理的话，或者说蝙蝠侠可能会有点力不从心。

sentences.en: Okay, that bad.
sentences.zh: 好吧，有那么糟。

sentences.en: So in Bushwick, I mean, we don't need to go through all the sort of stats and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以在布什威克，我是说，我们没必要去罗列那些统计数据什么的。

sentences.en: But all the descriptions of it are that in the center of the neighborhood, gangs are moving through within moments.
sentences.zh: 但所有的描述都显示，在社区中心，帮派转瞬间就在四处流窜。

sentences.en: It's as though they've been prepared, they've been ready, which, of course, they weren't.
sentences.zh: 就好像他们早有准备、蓄势待发一样——当然，他们其实并没有。

sentences.en: But people start moving through, looting shop after shop, they use trucks, they load furniture, hi-fis, televisions, all of these things.
sentences.zh: 但人们开始四处流动，一家接一家地抢劫店铺，他们用卡车装运家具、高保真音响、电视机以及所有这些东西。

sentences.en: I mean, the thing is that I remember living through the London riots in 2011, when basically, I mean, it was a kind of a frenzy of looting.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我记得自己经历过2011年的伦敦骚乱，当时基本上可以说是陷入了一种疯狂的抢劫狂潮。

sentences.en: And people just kind of got caught up on it.
sentences.zh: 人们不知不觉就被卷了进去。

sentences.en: It all seemed, everybody was just piling in.
sentences.zh: 似乎所有人都一拥而上。

sentences.en: And this is what happens, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上情况就是这样。

sentences.en: It is what happens.
sentences.zh: 确实就是这样。

sentences.en: So it's, I mean, here's one quote.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有一段引述。

sentences.en: People were grabbing shirts, pairs of pants, anything, running around and laughing.
sentences.zh: 人们抢夺衬衫、裤子以及任何东西，一边跑一边大笑。

sentences.en: It was as though they were suddenly free.
sentences.zh: 就好像他们突然获得了自由一样。

sentences.en: So that's a radio reporter who's up in Harlem.
sentences.zh: 这是一个在哈林区采访的电台记者说的。

sentences.en: This is a cop.
sentences.zh: 这是一位警察说的。

sentences.en: A cop says, the looters swept through here like locusts.
sentences.zh: 一个警察说，掠夺者像蝗虫一样席卷了这里。

sentences.en: I've seen looting before, but this was total devastation, smashing, burning as if people had gone crazy.
sentences.zh: 我以前见过抢劫，但这是彻底的毁灭，打砸、焚烧，就像人们疯了一样。

sentences.en: They were like bluefish in a feeding frenzy.
sentences.zh: 他们就像进入疯狂觅食状态的蓝鱼一样。

sentences.en: And it's not just, you know, the urban poor, is it?
sentences.zh: 而且不只是城市的穷人，对吧？

sentences.en: It's kind of affluent shoppers in midtown in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 还有曼哈顿中城富裕的购物者。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Kind of breaking in, grabbing pants.
sentences.zh: 他们也闯进去抢裤子。

sentences.en: I mean, you've got the story of a woman who's spotted stuffing a bag of ice into her very expensive designer handbag.
sentences.zh: 我是说，有个故事说，有人看到一个女人把一袋冰块塞进她那个非常昂贵的设计师手袋里。

sentences.en: Her Louis Vuitton handbag, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，是她的路易威登手袋。

sentences.en: She's stuffing a bag of ice into it.
sentences.zh: 她正把一袋冰块塞进去。

sentences.en: And the manager, or somebody sees, another customer sees her and says, I'll call the manager.
sentences.zh: 经理或者其他人看到了，另一个顾客看到她并说：我要叫经理。

sentences.en: And she drops it and flees.
sentences.zh: 于是她扔下包逃跑了。

sentences.en: But you think, what the hell, if she's got enough for a Louis Vuitton handbag?
sentences.zh: 但你会想，搞什么鬼，她既然买得起路易威登手袋？

sentences.en: I mean, this is very much a kind of Gotham City theme, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这非常具有哥谭市的色彩，对吧？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Of the crowds going wild.
sentences.zh: 那种人群陷入疯狂的景象。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's that fear that underpins so many stories about New York, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正是这种恐惧支撑了那么多关于纽约的故事。

sentences.en: The Batman story about Batman as the vigilante bringing order to this city that is permanently on the brink of anarchy.
sentences.zh: 关于蝙蝠侠的故事：蝙蝠侠作为一个义警，为这个永远处于无政府状态边缘的城市带来秩序。

sentences.en: And that has kind of currency because the NYPD, New York police, are overstretched and deeply mistrusted and kind of ravaged with corruption.
sentences.zh: 这种说法很有市场，因为纽约市警察局人手严重不足、极度不被信任，而且腐败横行。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so they also are not in a good state.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的状况也很不好。

sentences.en: They're in a terrible state.
sentences.zh: 他们的状况糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: And we'll get onto this in the second half, just why the NYPD are in such a terrible state in the 70s.
sentences.zh: 我们会在下半场讨论这个问题，说说为什么纽约市警察局在70年代会陷入如此糟糕的境地。

sentences.en: But to go back to Bushwick, this place, which is the absolute epitome, the embodiment, the symbol, the avatar of the lawlessness of that evening in the summer of 1977.
sentences.zh: 但回到布什威克，这个地方简直就是1977年那个夏夜无法无天状态的绝对缩影、化身、象征和代表。

sentences.en: The looting doesn't die down in Bushwick until just round about dawn.
sentences.zh: 布什威克的抢劫直到破晓时分才渐渐平息。

sentences.en: And when the sun rises, it reveals this neighborhood that has been, it's basically been gutted.
sentences.zh: 当太阳升起时，呈现在眼前的是一个基本上已经被洗劫一空的社区。

sentences.en: It's as though the people of the neighborhood have sacked their own city.
sentences.zh: 就好像这个社区的人洗劫了自己的城市一样。

sentences.en: Well, can I read from your book, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我能读一下你的书吗？

sentences.en: Please do, Tom.
sentences.zh: 请便，汤姆。

sentences.en: Do you think the listeners would like to hear more of your prose?
sentences.zh: 你觉得听众会想听更多你的散文吗？

sentences.en: They probably wouldn't, but I'm sure you're going to do it anyway.
sentences.zh: 他们可能不想，但我确信你无论如何都会读的。

sentences.en: Okay, I'm going to read it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我要读了。

sentences.en: So along Broadway, this is in Bushwick.
sentences.zh: 所以在百老汇大道沿线，这是在布什威克。

sentences.en: No fewer than 34 stores had been looted.
sentences.zh: 不少于34家店铺被抢。

sentences.en: 45 had also been set on fire.
sentences.zh: 45家店被纵火。

sentences.en: Most of Bushwick's buildings were made of timber and asphalt, a devastatingly flammable mixture.
sentences.zh: 布什威克的建筑大多由木材和沥青建成，这是一种极度易燃的混合物。

sentences.en: At one point, two entire blocks had been ablaze.
sentences.zh: 一度有整整两个街区陷入火海。

sentences.en: When fire crews had reached the scene, they had been bombarded with rocks and sticks by jeering looters.
sentences.zh: 当消防队员赶到现场时，遭到了一边发出嘲笑的暴徒投掷的石头和棍棒的袭击。

sentences.en: And the police had even resorted to using a water cannon to protect the firemen.
sentences.zh: 警察甚至不得不动用水炮来保护消防员。

sentences.en: Now, in the cold light of morning, 20 fires still burned and a cloud of black acrid smoke hung over the area.
sentences.zh: 现在，在清冷的晨光中，依然有20处大火在燃烧，一团刺鼻的黑烟笼罩在整个地区上空。

sentences.en: It was a scene from a war zone, a battlefield.
sentences.zh: 这是一幅战区、战场的景象。

sentences.en: It was a scene from the end of the world.
sentences.zh: 这是一幅世界末日的景象。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the potency of that scene from the point of view of those, you know, in the broader world is, again, that this is New York.
sentences.zh: 从广阔世界的角度来看，那个场景的冲击力再次在于，这里是纽约。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: There's a line by a guy, I think he's from the Miami Chamber of Commerce.
sentences.zh: 有一个家伙说了一句话，我想他是迈阿密商会的。

sentences.en: I was going to come up with it a bit later in the podcast, but it's appropriate now.
sentences.zh: 我本打算在播客稍后一点再提，但现在正合适。

sentences.en: He said, we knew exactly what to expect from New York and they didn't let us down, which I think is a very sort of telling moment.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们对纽约的期望可谓心知肚明，而他们也没有让我们失望。我认为这句话非常说明问题。

sentences.en: So to cut to the chase, more than almost 2,000 stores were looted.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，近2000家店铺遭到洗劫。

sentences.en: There were 1,000 fires across the city.
sentences.zh: 全市发生了1000起火灾。

sentences.en: Roughly 4,000 people were arrested.
sentences.zh: 大约有4000人被捕。

sentences.en: And that is merely a fraction of the numbers that could have been arrested.
sentences.zh: 而这仅仅是可能被捕人数中的一小部分。

sentences.en: The police at one point, Tom, are told to stop arresting people because they can't fit them into the cells.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，警察一度被告知停止抓人，因为他们塞不下号子里了。

sentences.en: And they're also told the time you're taking arresting people is time where you could have been on the streets.
sentences.zh: 他们还被告知，花在抓人上的时间本可以用来在街上巡逻。

sentences.en: So they just beat looters up.
sentences.zh: 所以他们索性直接暴打暴徒。

sentences.en: So they just say, go and crack heads.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只是说，去打爆他们的头吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Go and crack heads to try and stop it.
sentences.zh: 去打爆他们的头来试图阻止这一切。

sentences.en: So the costs are in the hundreds and hundreds of millions.
sentences.zh: 因此，损失高达数亿美元。

sentences.en: And when does the power cut finish?
sentences.zh: 停电是什么时候结束的？

sentences.en: So the power comes on the, towards the end of the following day.
sentences.zh: 电力在第二天快结束的时候恢复了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So the 14th.
sentences.zh: 也就是14号。

sentences.en: So there's only one night.
sentences.zh: 所以只有一晚。

sentences.en: So it's one night and the best part of one day.
sentences.zh: 所以是一晚加上整整一天的大部分时间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in intense heat, anyone who's been to New York in the summer, imagine what it's like with no air conditioning, no fans, just stifling, stifling heat.
sentences.zh: 而且是在酷热之中，任何去过夏天纽约的人都知道，想象一下没有空调、没有电扇，只有令人窒息的闷热是什么感觉。

sentences.en: And of course, for the press at the time, they see this as a symbol of all that's gone wrong with New York, which we'll get into.
sentences.zh: 当然，对于当时的媒体来说，他们将此视为纽约一切走向错误的象征，我们接下来会探讨这一点。

sentences.en: And there's one paper in particular, which we should talk about, which is the New York Post, whose headline is 24 Hours of Terror.
sentences.zh: 有一家报纸尤其值得我们讨论，那就是《纽约邮报》，其头条是《恐怖24小时》。

sentences.en: It's a banner headline.
sentences.zh: 这是一个通栏大标题。

sentences.en: And why the New York Post?
sentences.zh: 为什么是《纽约邮报》？

sentences.en: Because the New York Post, just a few months earlier, had been taken over.
sentences.zh: 因为《纽约邮报》在几个月前刚刚被收购。

sentences.en: By Logan Roy.
sentences.zh: 被洛根·罗伊。

sentences.en: By Logan Roy.
sentences.zh: 被洛根·罗伊。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the New York Post, a newspaper founded by hip-hop star Alexander Hamilton, had been taken over by Rupert Murdoch.
sentences.zh: 所以，《纽约邮报》这份由嘻哈明星亚历山大·汉密尔顿创立的报纸，被鲁伯特·默多克收购了。

sentences.en: So Logan Roy is the fictional incarnation of Rupert Murdoch in Succession, the TV drama.
sentences.zh: 所以洛根·罗伊就是电视剧《继承之战》中鲁伯特·默多克的虚构化身。

sentences.en: So British listeners will know Rupert Murdoch very well, as of course our American listeners will too.
sentences.zh: 因此英国听众对鲁伯特·默多克会非常熟悉，我们的美国听众当然也是如此。

sentences.en: At the time, British newspaper readers would have known his name because he was the owner of The Sun.
sentences.zh: 在当时，英国报纸读者会知道他的名字，因为他是《太阳报》的老板。

sentences.en: He's Australian, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他是澳大利亚人，对吧？

sentences.en: He's Australian, the most aggressive tabloid, the most popular tabloid that someone should.
sentences.zh: 他是澳大利亚人，拥有最激进、最受欢迎的小报，某人应该……

sentences.en: That year, 1976, at the time when he took over The Post, had just overtaken The Mirror to become the biggest-selling newspaper in Britain.
sentences.zh: 那一年，即1976年，在他接手《邮报》时，《太阳报》刚刚超越《每日镜报》，成为英国销量最大的报纸。

sentences.en: Now, at the time, people said Murdoch will never hack it in America.
sentences.zh: 当时，人们说默多克在美国永远混不下去。

sentences.en: He won't be a success.
sentences.zh: 他不会成功的。

sentences.en: We won't like his formula.
sentences.zh: 我们不会喜欢他的那一套。

sentences.en: And they were, of course, completely wrong.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们完全大错特错了。

sentences.en: So The Post, which was a kind of working-class, democratic newspaper, he said, we need to beef this up.
sentences.zh: 所以对于《邮报》这份面向工人阶级的民主派报纸，他说，我们需要加强内容。

sentences.en: What our readers want, they want a lot of stuff about crime.
sentences.zh: 我们的读者想看的是大量关于犯罪的内容。

sentences.en: They want scandals.
sentences.zh: 他们想看丑闻。

sentences.en: They don't have the page three topless.
sentences.zh: 美国可没有第三页的半裸照。

sentences.en: They don't have topless girls in America.
sentences.zh: 美国没有半裸女郎。

sentences.en: Which is a notorious thing that The Sun has.
sentences.zh: 这是《太阳报》出了名的一大特色。

sentences.en: Which, yeah, The Sun had in Britain.
sentences.zh: 是的，《太阳报》在英国就是这样。

sentences.en: Everybody attacks Murdoch and says he's a carpetbagger.
sentences.zh: 所有人都在攻击默多克，说他是投机分子。

sentences.en: Who cares about Australians?
sentences.zh: 谁在乎澳大利亚人？

sentences.en: He brings in loads of British and Australian journalists to run The New York Post, which is very controversial among American journalists.
sentences.zh: 他带了大量英国和澳大利亚记者来运营《纽约邮报》，这在美籍记者中引发了极大争议。

sentences.en: Because the London newspaper scene is actually much more competitive than the New York scene.
sentences.zh: 因为伦敦的报业竞争其实比纽约激烈得多。

sentences.en: Much more competitive.
sentences.zh: 竞争激烈得多。

sentences.en: And frankly, Tom, much more exciting.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，汤姆，也刺激得多。

sentences.en: You know, much because it's more cutthroats, you get better papers.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，因为更加残酷，所以你能看到更好的报纸。

sentences.en: And to Murdoch, the New York scene is very staid.
sentences.zh: 而在默多克看来，纽约的报业显得十分沉闷。

sentences.en: And so he and The Post seize on the blackout.
sentences.zh: 因此他和《邮报》紧紧抓住了这次大停电。

sentences.en: And they run story after story, front page after front page.
sentences.zh: 他们接连报道了一个又一个故事，头版接头版。

sentences.en: And it sells kind of massively.
sentences.zh: 销量暴增。

sentences.en: They sold tens of thousands of extra copies based on their coverage of the blackout.
sentences.zh: 凭借对大停电的报道，他们多售出了几万份报纸。

sentences.en: So, Rupert Murdoch is, I mean, he's very conservative.
sentences.zh: 所以，鲁伯特·默多克这个人，非常保守。

sentences.en: He's very much on the right.
sentences.zh: 他非常右倾。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, is he going in with a kind of law and order, string them up kind of approach?
sentences.zh: 所以，他是不是带着一种强调法律与秩序、把他们统统绞死的态度入场的？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 千真万确。

sentences.zh: 如果你早二十年出生，你就不会这么想了。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because New York in the 50s and 60s was perceived abroad and in America as the epitome of everything that was most glamorous, most dazzling about American life.
sentences.zh: 因为在五六十年代，无论是在海外还是在美国本土，纽约都被视为美国生活中最迷人、最耀眼的一切的缩影。

sentences.en: It's Don Draper in Mad Men.
sentences.zh: 就像《广告狂人》里的唐·德雷珀。

sentences.en: It's people drinking martinis.
sentences.zh: 就像人们在喝着马提尼。

sentences.en: It's breakfast at Tiffany's.
sentences.zh: 就像《蒂凡尼的早餐》。

sentences.en: Audrey Hepburn.
sentences.zh: 就像奥黛丽·赫本。

sentences.en: If you've ever seen, lots of our listeners would have seen North by NorthweSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你看过的话——我们的很多听众应该都看过《西北偏北》。

sentences.en: You know, Cary Grant.
sentences.zh: 你知道，加里·格兰特。

sentences.en: The cool of the city.
sentences.zh: 那种城市的酷炫。

sentences.en: The stylish lines of the buildings.
sentences.zh: 建筑时髦的线条。

sentences.en: Sharp suits.
sentences.zh: 利落的西装。

sentences.en: Sharp suits.
sentences.zh: 利落的西装。

sentences.en: Great dresses.
sentences.zh: 漂亮的裙子。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: And that begins to change, I would say, towards the end of the 60s.
sentences.zh: 我想，这种情况大约从六十年代末开始发生变化。

sentences.en: So, at the beginning of 1966, New York gets a new mayor who's called John Vliet Lindsay.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1966年初，纽约迎来了新市长，名叫约翰·弗利特·林赛。

sentences.en: He is the person for whom the phrase, which some of our American listeners will be familiar with, limousine liberal, was applied to.
sentences.zh: 有些美国听众可能会熟悉“豪华轿车自由派”这个词，而这个词最初就是用来形容他的。

sentences.en: And he is the absolute personification of kind of patrician, old money, the old elite, if you like.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是那种贵族气派、老钱阶层、旧精英的化身。

sentences.en: An elite that you can sort of trace back to the novels of Henry James and Edith Wharton, kind of gilded age in New York.
sentences.zh: 这种精英阶层，你甚至可以追溯到亨利·詹姆斯和伊迪丝·华顿的小说里那种纽约的镀金时代。

sentences.en: So, Lindsay went to a boarding school.
sentences.zh: 所以，林赛上过寄宿学校。

sentences.en: Americans don't often talk about this, but a large part of their elite go to boarding schools.
sentences.zh: 美国人平时不太常谈论这个，但他们很大一部分精英确实都出身于寄宿学校。

sentences.en: So, Lindsay went to a boarding school and he went to Yale.
sentences.zh: 所以，林赛上过寄宿学校，后来又上了耶鲁大学。

sentences.en: He's a very JFK-ish figure.
sentences.zh: 他是个很有肯尼迪风格的人物。

sentences.en: He's young, handsome, sporty, civilized.
sentences.zh: 年轻、帅气、热爱运动、举止文雅。

sentences.en: And in this symbolic moment, on the day he takes office, there's a transport strike and he has to walk to work.
sentences.zh: 而在一个具有象征意义的时刻，在他上任的第一天，发生了交通罢工，他不得不步行去上班。

sentences.en: And that sets the tone for the whole of his administration.
sentences.zh: 这也为他整个任期定下了基调。

sentences.en: So, there's constant strikes, money problems, rising crime.
sentences.zh: 因此，罢工不断、资金短缺、犯罪率上升。

sentences.en: And actually, the issue is that something has gone badly wrong for New York as it has for so many American cities in the 60s.
sentences.zh: 事实上，核心问题在于，就像六十年代的许多美国城市一样，纽约出了大问题。

sentences.en: And actually, that anticipates what's going to happen to lots of cities elsewhere in the
sentences.zh: 而这其实也预示了接下来将要发生在

sentences.en: Western world.
sentences.zh: 西方世界许多城市的情况。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, with your Marxist hat on.
sentences.zh: 那么，换上你的马克思主义视角。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: What is happening is the expression of very, very deep-seated economic revulsions and changes.
sentences.zh: 正在发生的是非常、非常深层的经济激变和变革的体现。

sentences.en: So, what are they?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些变革是什么呢？

sentences.en: So, the flight of manufacturing.
sentences.zh: 制造业的外流。

sentences.en: New York had been a great manufacturing city.
sentences.zh: 纽约曾是一座伟大的制造业城市。

sentences.en: The garment district in New York is the great symbol of that.
sentences.zh: 纽约的服装区就是其中最伟大的象征。

sentences.en: People making all these clothes.
sentences.zh: 人们在那里制作各种各样的衣服。

sentences.en: Well, that's been outsourced.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些现在都外包了。

sentences.en: And it's happening abroad.
sentences.zh: 而且正发生在海外。

sentences.en: Suburbanization.
sentences.zh: 郊区化。

sentences.en: White, middle-class people, in particular, are moving out to the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 尤其是白人中产阶级，正纷纷搬往郊区。

sentences.en: But also, there's a big shift in America, generally, from what's called the Rust Belt.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，整个美国还发生了一个重大转变，也就是从所谓的“铁锈地带”转移。

sentences.en: So, those are the old industrial heartlands.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些老牌的工业腹地。

sentences.en: Detroit is the kind of classic exemplification.
sentences.zh: 底特律就是最典型的代表。

sentences.en: Detroit, Pittsburgh, Cleveland, Cincinnati.
sentences.zh: 底特律、匹兹堡、克利夫兰、辛辛那提。

sentences.en: Great cities.
sentences.zh: 伟大的城市。

sentences.en: Great cities that have been the powerhouse of America.
sentences.zh: 这些曾是美国发展引擎的伟大城市。

sentences.en: But in the 70s, the booming cities are Dallas, Phoenix.
sentences.zh: 但在七十年代，蓬勃发展的城市变成了达拉斯、菲尼克斯。

sentences.en: Because they've suddenly got air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 因为它们突然有了空调。

sentences.en: Because they've got air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 因为它们有了空调。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it seems like such a banal thing, but air conditioning is one of the great transformative moments in American demographic history.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来像是一件微不足道的事，但空调却是美国人口统计史上最具变革性的伟大时刻之一。

sentences.en: Because now you can go and establish factories in the South and Southwest, where, by the way, they have quite restrictive anti-union laws.
sentences.zh: 因为现在你可以在南方和西南部建立工厂了，顺便说一句，那里有相当严格的反工会法律。

sentences.en: So, for an employer, it actually makes sense.
sentences.zh: 所以对雇主来说，这确实合情合理。

sentences.en: But also, isn't there also a sense that you can build factories and things from scratch there?
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，是不是也有一种感觉，就是你可以在那里从头开始建设工厂之类的一切？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Whereas, in a city like New York, the infrastructure will often be quite antiquated.
sentences.zh: 而在纽约这样的城市，基础设施往往相当陈旧过时。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's crumbling, crumbling infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 基础设施正在崩溃、崩塌。

sentences.en: Crumbling infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 崩溃的基础设施。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, lots of, particularly, sort of more affluent, more educated, white families moving out of New York, and lots of new people moving in.
sentences.zh: 因此，许多相对富裕、受教育程度更高、特别是白人家庭正在搬离纽约，同时有大量新人搬进来。

sentences.en: And these are...
sentences.zh: 而这些人是……

sentences.en: But this is, I mean, this is nothing new.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，这其实并不是什么新鲜事。

sentences.en: The whole thing about New York, the Statue of Liberty, huddled masses, all that kind, is that waves and waves of immigration come in, and the city gives them jobs.
sentences.zh: 纽约的全部意义——自由女神像、拥挤的底层民众诸如此类——就是一波又一波的移民涌入，而这座城市为他们提供了工作。

sentences.en: But is it the case, in the 70s, that for the first time, there aren't the jobs available?
sentences.zh: 但在七十年代，情况是不是第一次出现没有足够的工作岗位可供选择了？

sentences.en: There are two things.
sentences.zh: 这里有两个因素。

sentences.en: One, there is a class of people that have always been there in New York, who are now leaving, who are the more affluent people.
sentences.zh: 第一，纽约一直存在的一个阶层——那些比较富裕的人——现在正在离开。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Or, sort of, somewhere like Brooklyn, or the Bronx, even, white, working-class, kind of,
sentences.zh: 或者说，像布鲁克林，甚至布朗克斯，白人工人阶层那种……

sentences.en: in inverted commas, and this is, I know it's a heavy-loaded word, sort of respectable working-class families.
sentences.zh: 打着引号的——我知道这是一个很沉重的词——某种体面的工人阶层家庭。

sentences.en: Whereas, they are moving out to the suburbs, and the people who are moving...
sentences.zh: 然而，当他们搬往郊区时，搬进来的人却是……

sentences.en: To New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 搬到新泽西。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: To purpose-built estates and things.
sentences.zh: 搬进专门建造的住宅区之类的地方。

sentences.en: Whereas, the people who are moving in, there are lots of migrants from the Caribbean, from
sentences.zh: 然而搬进来的人，有大量来自加勒比海、

sentences.en: Central America, from Puerto Rico, or African-Americans from the South.
sentences.zh: 中美洲、波多黎各的移民，或者是来自南方的非裔美国人。

sentences.en: Now, in the past, as you said, loads of such people arrived in New York City, but there were jobs.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，过去有大批这样的人来到纽约市，但当时有工作可做。

sentences.en: But, actually, now, there are not jobs.
sentences.zh: 然而现在，确实没有工作了。

sentences.en: The economic obstacles to the newcomers are much greater than ever before.
sentences.zh: 新来者面临的经济障碍比以往任何时候都要大得多。

sentences.en: So, in the month of the blackout, July 1977, seven out of ten African-Americans in New
sentences.zh: 因此，在大停电发生的那个月，即1977年7月，纽约十分之七的非裔美国人和

sentences.en: York are out of work, and eight out of ten of the Hispanic population.
sentences.zh: 十分之八的西班牙裔人口都处于失业状态。

sentences.en: So, massive, massive unemployment rates.
sentences.zh: 所以，失业率高得惊人。

sentences.en: Now, as a result of that, you get into a vicious spiral.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为结果，你陷入了一种恶性循环。

sentences.en: And, Tom, I warn you, there's going to be a tiny, tiny bit of economics.
sentences.zh: 而且，汤姆，我得警告你，接下来要讲一点点、一点点的经济学。

sentences.en: Oh, goodness.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: So, we've had industry, and now we've got economics.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们刚聊完工业，现在又要聊经济学了。

sentences.en: Well, we've had the analysis of electricity generation, and now of tax bases.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们之前分析了发电量，现在要分析税基了。

sentences.en: Because, of course, when you've got high unemployment, you've got fewer people paying a lot of tax, but you also have much bigger welfare roles.
sentences.zh: 因为当然，当失业率很高时，交大笔税的人变少了，但你需要负担的社会福利开支却大大增加了。

sentences.en: So, what you have is that New York is making less money, but it's liabilities.
sentences.zh: 所以出现的情况是，纽约赚的钱变少了，但它的负债却……

sentences.en: But having to spend more.
sentences.zh: 却不得不花得更多。

sentences.en: And having to spend more.
sentences.zh: 而且不得不花得更多。

sentences.en: And that's not just New York.
sentences.zh: 而且不只是纽约这样。

sentences.en: So, Boston, Chicago, Detroit, Pittsburgh, some of those cities we mentioned.
sentences.zh: 波士顿、芝加哥、底特律、匹兹堡，我们刚才提到的一些城市也是如此。

sentences.en: Well, Detroit, I mean, is basically collapsing.
sentences.zh: 底特律嘛，基本上正在崩溃。

sentences.en: Well, it's not yet collapsing, but it's approaching the brink of it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，虽然还没完全崩溃，但也正逼近崩溃的边缘。

sentences.en: So, they're running up tens and tens of millions of debts.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们积累了数以千万计的巨额债务。

sentences.en: But nowhere is it worse than in New York.
sentences.zh: 但没有哪个地方比纽约更糟糕了。

sentences.en: So, the mayoralty of that guy that I mentioned, John Lindsay, ends up in a complete sort of disaster as he runs into financial probleMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，我刚才提到的那个家伙——约翰·林赛的市长任期，在陷入财务困境后，最终以彻底的灾难告终。

sentences.en: The city is losing hundreds of thousands of jobs every year.
sentences.zh: 这座城市每年都在失去几十万个工作岗位。

sentences.en: The deficit is getting bigger and bigger.
sentences.zh: 财政赤字越来越大。

sentences.en: So, in 1974, when Lindsay gives way to a new mayor, already the city has this reputation as a financial basket case.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1974年林赛卸任并将权力移交给新市长时，这座城市已经落得个财政彻底失败的坏名声。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the New York Times itself, Tom, talking about its own city in 1974.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是《纽约时报》自己在1974年对这座城市做出的评价，汤姆。

sentences.en: New York City has become a metaphor for what looks like the last days of American civilization.
sentences.zh: 纽约市已经成了美国文明末日景象的代名词。

sentences.en: It's run by fools.
sentences.zh: 它由一群傻瓜统治。

sentences.en: It's citizens at the mercy of its criminals, who often as not are protected by an unholy alliance of civil libertarians and crooked cops.
sentences.zh: 市民们任由罪灵摆布，而这些罪犯往往受到民权自由主义者和腐败警察的罪恶同盟的庇护。

sentences.en: The air is foul, the traffic is impossible, services are diminishing, and the morale is such that ordering a cup of coffee in a diner can turn into a request for a fat lip.
sentences.zh: 空气污浊，交通瘫痪，公共服务日益萎缩，士气低落到在小餐馆里点杯咖啡都可能招来一顿老拳。

sentences.en: New York City is a mess, and it's getting worse all the time.
sentences.zh: 纽约市一团糟，而且情况还在不断恶化。

sentences.en: So, great stuff for the New York tourist board.
sentences.zh: 这对于纽约旅游局来说可真是绝佳的宣传材料啊。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a great advert for the city.
sentences.zh: 对啊，这对这座城市来说是个极好的广告。

sentences.en: January 74, a new mayor comes in, and he's basically a symbol of New York.
sentences.zh: 1974年1月，新市长上任，他基本上成了纽约的象征。

sentences.en: He's a guy, he's very short, he's called Abraham Beam.
sentences.zh: 他个子很矮，名叫亚伯拉罕·比姆。

sentences.en: And he is the son of Jewish immigrants from Poland.
sentences.zh: 他是来自波兰的犹太移民的儿子。

sentences.en: And classic kind of people that you'd get, they're moving to the Lower East Side, where so many Eastern European Jewish immigrants did.
sentences.zh: 属于那种典型的人群，他们搬到了下东区，许多东欧犹太移民都曾落脚于此。

sentences.en: He was born in 1906.
sentences.zh: 他出生于1906年。

sentences.en: Like so many bright Jewish poor boys, he benefited from free education at the City College of New York.
sentences.zh: 像许多聪明的贫寒犹太男孩一样，他受益于纽约城市学院的免费教育。

sentences.en: And then he became a democratic kind of machine politician.
sentences.zh: 后来他成了一名民主党机器政治家。

sentences.en: He was the financial controller.
sentences.zh: 他曾担任财务审计长。

sentences.en: So, he's meant to be the person with the figures.
sentences.zh: 所以，他本该是个精通数字的人。

sentences.en: He becomes mayor.
sentences.zh: 他当选为市长。

sentences.en: When he comes in, the city is facing a complete financial meltdown.
sentences.zh: 当他上任时，这座城市正面临全面的金融崩盘。

sentences.en: So, he is basically having to borrow money at rates of 10%, interest rates of 10%, just to pay the city's workers.
sentences.zh: 因此，他基本上不得不以10%的高利率借钱，仅仅为了支付城市工人的工资。

sentences.en: Which presumably include cops, firemen, and people who collect the litter.
sentences.zh: 想必这其中包含了警察、消防员以及清扫垃圾的环卫工人。

sentences.en: All of those things.
sentences.zh: 所有这些人都包括在内。

sentences.en: All of those things.
sentences.zh: 所有这些人。

sentences.en: But, people won't lend him the money.
sentences.zh: 但是，人们不肯借钱给他。

sentences.en: By the spring of 1975, he's basically staring into the abyss.
sentences.zh: 到1975年春天，他基本上已经走投无路、濒临深渊了。

sentences.en: He gets a loan from the state, New York State, but that even won't cover his own payroll.
sentences.zh: 他从纽约州得到了贷款，但这甚至无法支付市政员工的薪水。

sentences.en: So, he has to go to the federal government.
sentences.zh: 所以，他不得不向联邦政府求助。

sentences.en: Ronald Reagan, Tom, your mate, who you impersonate so well.
sentences.zh: 罗纳德·里根，汤姆，你的好朋友，你模仿得维妙维肖的那个人。

sentences.en: Ronald Reagan said, New York can just save itself.
sentences.zh: 罗纳德·里根说，纽约可以自己拯救自己。

sentences.en: He said, New York must prove that it can handle itself.
sentences.zh: 他说，纽约必须证明自己有能力处理好自己的事情。

sentences.en: We shouldn't lend them any money.
sentences.zh: 我们不应该借给他们任何钱。

sentences.en: But, Ronald Reagan's rival, Gerald Ford, his president, he obviously can't really allow the city to sink.
sentences.zh: 但是，罗纳德·里根的竞争对手、时任总统杰拉尔德·福特，显然不能真的眼睁睁看着这座城市沉没。

sentences.en: But, there is a famous headline, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 不过，当时有一个著名的头条新闻，对吧？

sentences.en: There is.
sentences.zh: 确实有。

sentences.en: In the New York PoSt.
sentences.zh: 刊登在《纽约邮报》上。

sentences.en: In the New York Post, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，刊登在《纽约邮报》上。

sentences.en: Ford to city, drop dead, was the headline.
sentences.zh: 头条标题就是：福特对这座城市说，去死吧。

sentences.en: Because they've asked him for a loan.
sentences.zh: 因为他们向他申请了一笔贷款。

sentences.en: They've asked him for a bailout, and he said no initially.
sentences.zh: 他们向他请求提供紧急财政援助，而他最初拒绝了。

sentences.en: Actually, that's a bit unfair on Ford, because Ford does change his mind.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这对福特来说有点不公平，因为福特确实改变了主意。

sentences.en: He gives them a $2 billion loan guarantee bailout.
sentences.zh: 他给予了他们20亿美元的贷款担保救助。

sentences.en: Because, if he didn't, the city would have collapsed.
sentences.zh: 因为如果他不这么做，这座城市就会崩溃。

sentences.zh: 汤姆，他认为重建城市的方法之一，就是给私人开发商更大的自由度。

sentences.en: Private, I have a hunch where you're going with this.
sentences.zh: 私人开发商，我有预感你接下来要说什么了。

sentences.en: So, I mentioned developers.
sentences.zh: 所以，我提到了开发商。

sentences.en: This is the other thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是另一回事了。

sentences.en: One man's crisis is another man's opportunity.
sentences.zh: 一个人的危机就是另一个人的机遇。

sentences.en: So as New York declines, decays, you've got burned out hotels and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 所以随着纽约的衰落和腐朽，到处都是烧毁的酒店和诸如此类的情形。

sentences.en: Some people see in this a chance to make some money.
sentences.zh: 有些人从中看到了赚钱的机会。

sentences.en: Now, there's one place in particular where they see it.
sentences.zh: 现在，有一个地方是他们特别看重的。

sentences.en: This is a corner of Midtown Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 这就是曼哈顿中城的一个角落。

sentences.en: It's right next to Grand Central Station.
sentences.zh: 它就在中央车站旁边。

sentences.en: Grand Central, of course, decaying at the time, but a symbol of an earlier golden age kind of New York.
sentences.zh: 中央车站当时当然也在走向衰败，但它某种程度上是早期纽约黄金时代的一个象征。

sentences.en: So on East 42nd Street between Lexington and Park Avenue, not a million miles from where we are now, there was a hotel called the Commodore.
sentences.zh: 所以在莱克星顿大道和公园大道之间的东42街上，离我们现在的位置不远，曾有一家名为康莫多尔的酒店。

sentences.en: And it had been owned by the Penn Central Railroad, which had gone bust in 1976.
sentences.zh: 它曾由宾州中央铁路公司所有，该公司已于1976年破产。

sentences.en: And the hotel was derelict.
sentences.zh: 而这家酒店当时已经废弃。

sentences.en: At the time of the blackout, the hotel is completely derelict.
sentences.zh: 在大停电期间，这家酒店已经彻底荒废。

sentences.en: There are rats in the basement.
sentences.zh: 地下室里有老鼠。

sentences.en: A lot of the rooms have been taken over by prostitutes.
sentences.zh: 许多房间都被妓女占领了。

sentences.en: Supervillains are plotting death rays in the basement.
sentences.zh: 超级反派正在地下室里密谋死亡射线。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: All that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事。

sentences.en: And there's sort of drug dealers everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是毒贩。

sentences.en: It is this sort of vision of an urban hell.
sentences.zh: 这简直就是城市地狱的景象。

sentences.en: And one ambitious young developer, Tom, I wonder if you can possibly guess who it is, sees this and he thinks he can turn it around.
sentences.zh: 而一个雄心勃勃的年轻开发商，汤姆，我不知道你能不能猜到他是谁，看到了这一切，他觉得自己能扭转乾坤。

sentences.en: So he does a deal with the Defunct Railroad and with the Hyatt Hotel Corporation.
sentences.zh: 于是他与破产的铁路公司以及凯悦酒店集团达成了一笔交易。

sentences.en: And crucially, he needs a tax deal from Abraham Beam, from the outgoing mayor.
sentences.zh: 最关键的是，他需要时任市长亚伯拉罕·贝姆给予税收优惠政策。

sentences.en: As luck would have it, his father has precisely the contacts he needs.
sentences.zh: 说来也巧，他的父亲正好拥有他需要的人脉。

sentences.en: And Beam and the city give him a 40-year tax break to redevelop this hotel.
sentences.zh: 贝姆和市政府给了他40年的税收减免，用来重新开发这家酒店。

sentences.en: So a few months after the blackout, in the summer of 1978, well, a year after the blackout, I should say,
sentences.zh: 所以在大停电几个月后，在1978年夏天，好吧，应该说在大停电一年后，

sentences.en: he starts work on it and it opens in September 1980, just weeks before the election of Ronald Reagan.
sentences.zh: 他开始着手改造，酒店于1980年9月开业，就在罗纳德·里根竞选总统几周前。

sentences.en: I mean, the timing is unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这时间简直不可思议。

sentences.en: It opens as the Hyatt Grand Central Hotel.
sentences.zh: 它作为凯悦中央车站酒店重新开业。

sentences.en: And it's a new kind of hotel covered with shimmering glass.
sentences.zh: 这是一种新型酒店，外墙贴满了闪闪发光的玻璃。

sentences.en: Lots of bling.
sentences.zh: 充满了暴发户气息。

sentences.en: Very blingy.
sentences.zh: 非常奢华耀眼。

sentences.en: Gold fittings.
sentences.zh: 金色的配件。

sentences.en: Absolutely massive atrium, fountains.
sentences.zh: 极其巨大的中庭，还有喷泉。

sentences.en: So it's right on the cusp of the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 所以它正处于20世纪80年代的边缘。

sentences.en: And it is this temple to what you mentioned, the bonfire of the vanities, 80s excess.
sentences.zh: 这就是你提到的那个庙宇——《虚荣的篝火》、80年代的过度放纵。

sentences.en: Now, one last thing.
sentences.zh: 现在，还有最后一点。

sentences.en: That tax break that I mentioned, that his dad got him, it costs the city of New York $410 million.
sentences.zh: 我刚才提到的那个他父亲帮他争取的税收减免，让纽约市损失了4.1亿美元。

sentences.en: That's the art of the deal, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 这就是交易的艺术，多米尼克。

sentences.en: That is the art of the deal.
sentences.zh: 这就是交易的艺术。

sentences.en: That's the art of the deal.
sentences.zh: 这就是交易的艺术。

sentences.en: And Tom, the name of that young developer.
sentences.zh: 那么汤姆，那个年轻开发商的名字是……

sentences.en: Should you leave it hanging?
sentences.zh: 你要把它悬念留到最后吗？

sentences.en: Well, if you can't guess by now, should I put them out of their misery?
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果你现在还猜不到，我是不是该让他们解脱了？

sentences.en: It is, of course, Donald J.
sentences.zh: 他当然就是唐纳德·J·

sentences.en: Trump.
sentences.zh: 特朗普。

sentences.en: And on that bombshell, on that bombshell, we will bid farewell to Gotham City in the 70s.
sentences.zh: 带着这个重磅炸弹，带着这个重磅炸弹，我们要向70年代的哥谭市道别了。

sentences.en: On the cusp of the 80s.
sentences.zh: 正处于80年代的边缘。

sentences.en: So, yeah, so I think that we should definitely do New York in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，所以我觉得我们绝对应该做一期关于80年代纽约的节目。

sentences.en: It's such a great subject.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常棒的主题。

sentences.en: I mean, as iconic as New York in the 70s, really.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它其实和70年代的纽约一样具有标志性。

sentences.en: So thank you, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆。

sentences.en: Why don't we go down to the Hyatt Grand Central and I'll buy you a martini.
sentences.zh: 要不我们去凯悦中央车站，我请你喝马提尼。

sentences.en: That would be fantastic.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。

sentences.en: We'll head there.
sentences.zh: 我们这就过去。

sentences.en: See you all very soon.
sentences.zh: 祝大家很快再见。

sentences.en: Hope you've enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 希望你们喜欢。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。
